summary: Rebecca Redwood French works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned a J.D. at the University of Washington and an LL.M. and Ph.D. at Yale under Leopold Pospisil, Stanley Weinstein, Harold C. Conklin, Mirjan Damaška, and Robert A. F. Thurman.
Rebecca Sundén is an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied and worked as a Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

Reginald A. Ray is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under teachers including Mircea Eliade and Joseph Kitagawa, and served as Professor in Buddhist Studies at Naropa University (attested 2001–2006).
Rei Yoshimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Waseda University from circa 1949 to 1953 and later served there as a professor from circa 1970 to 2000.
Reiho Masunaga was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Kaiten Nukariya. He taught at Komazawa University from circa 1945 to 1972.

Reiko Ohnuma specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. She studied at UC Berkeley and earned a Ph.D. at the University of Michigan under Luis O. Gómez, later joining the faculty at Dartmouth College (attested 2012).

Reimon Yuki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Daijo Tokiwa (~1924–1927). He held appointments at the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia, the University of Tokyo, and Kyoto Women's University.

Reiner Wiehl was a philosopher who completed a Diplomarbeit at the University of Nancy and a PhD at Goethe University Frankfurt. He served as professor of philosophy at the University of Hamburg (1969–1977) and Heidelberg University (appointed 1977).
Reinhold Grünendahl is an Indologist who held posts at Freie Universität Berlin (attested 1983) and the Göttingen State and University Library (attested 2008).

Reinhold Klotz was a scholar in linguistics, history, and archaeology. After completing his Habilitation at the University of Leipzig (1826–1831), he served there as assistant professor from 1832 and as außerordentlicher Professor from 1849 to 1870.

Reinhold Niebuhr was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Elmhurst University, Eden Theological Seminary, and Yale Divinity School (~1913–1915), later serving on the faculty of Union Theological Seminary from circa 1928 to 1960.

Reinhold Rost was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who earned a Ph.D. at the University of Jena. He held teaching posts in Canterbury, served as secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society, and became head librarian at the India Office.
Reirin Yamada was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University from circa 1911 to 1914 and later served as president of Komazawa Junior College.

Reita Nakamura is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies and served as a graduate student researcher at Toyo University (attested 2015), as well as a researcher at the Shinshu Otani-ha Shinran Buddhist Center (attested 2015).
Remeen Firoz is an Indology scholar pursuing a PhD at the Australian National University under the supervision of Assa Doron (attested 2026).

Renate Syed is an Indologist who earned her doctorate at the University of Munich (~1974–1982) under Dieter Schlingloff. She serves as a Privatdozentin at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).
Renda Zheng is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under traditional teachers Kai Zhi, Shengfa, and Kai Tong.
Renjo Akamatsu was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Chō Sanshū and held a post at Ryukoku University.
René Gothóni is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Helsinki (~1970–1982) and held an academic post there from circa 1977 to 2014.

René Grousset was a scholar of history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and sinology who studied at the University of Montpellier. He held posts at Musée Guimet, École du Louvre, Musée Cernuschi, and the Louvre Museum.
